answer: Mechanism: cohort-gated admission. Each cohort's fee equals its predecessor's payouts per slot; inflow inflates the next fee. In tundra windows, when demand is sparse, fees freeze so newcomers stay cheap. Each paid slot binds to a cipher: the hash of an agent's key plus cohort epoch, on an append-only chain, so identities cannot be reset or split in parallel. Attack cost: N sybils pay N cohort fees, rising linearly with cohort size, burned, never refunded. New agents start on a narrow revenue ledge, a tier capped below veterans. Honest users pay once.
